findings.problem: In the qa_rule_ref.quote for CLAIM-02, the fragment after '...' ('An item already fulfilled in Shopify gets its design re-generated: it stays fulfilled and does not move back to Ready.') is the submitter's join of the rule's example when/then. It is not a literal substring of the spec-hub capture (where 'then' starts 'It stays...'). The capture note still says 'phần trích khớp nguyên văn'.
findings.evidence: Fragment found in _ccr-full-content.md: True. Found in raw/ccr-evidence/CBS-138__CLAIM-02/spec-hub-design-generation-ready.json: False. The capture holds examples[0].when + examples[0].then. Meaning is identical (live text confirmed, spec-hub log 212/210).
findings.required_fix: No publish change: the gate accepts a substring of _ccr-full-content.md, and KB-782 does not carry the quote. In future intake, record in the capture note that the quote joins rule + example, rather than calling it verbatim.

findings.problem: The S2 elements are met only loosely. §12.3a defines S2 as an owned QA rule with a code in the QA store and an owner by role. Here the code is a spec-hub rule id, owner_role is 'code (spec-hub reads teeinblue-api source)' (not a QA owner role), and recorded_on is the query date. The practice of treating spec-hub rules as S2 is not written in the contract or in DECISIONS.md.
findings.evidence: qa_rule_ref.owner_role and code on all four claims. Same pattern already published under CBS-132/CBS-136 (e.g. knowledge/products/teeinblue/font/features/upload-custom-font/kb.json KB-022). The outcome is conservative: PROPOSED/LOW, never an oracle, Dev/PO OQ attached.
findings.required_fix: Not blocking for this run (consistent with published precedent). Ask the operator whether to ratify 'spec-hub rule = S2, owner_role code' in DECISIONS.md and, if so, add it to ccr-protocol.md §12.3a, so later reviewers stop judging it case by case.
